checks.description: Infrastructure and deployments are defined as code / automated, not manual console changes.
Monitoring, logging, and alerting are defined for the workload's key operational signals.
An incident response process or runbook is referenced for operational failures.
Changes can be rolled back safely; deployment approach limits blast radius of a bad change.
IAM roles/permissions follow least privilege rather than broad/wildcard access.
Sensitive or PII-bearing data stores have encryption at rest specified.
Data in transit is encrypted (TLS) between components, especially over public networks.
Credentials/API keys/secrets are managed via a secrets store, not hardcoded or embedded in config.
Network boundaries/segmentation are defined; public-facing components are minimized and fronted appropriately.
Authentication/authorization (SSO, MFA, RBAC) is defined for user- and system-facing access.
Security-relevant actions and access are logged in an auditable, tamper-resistant way.
Critical components have redundancy (multi-AZ or equivalent) rather than a single point of failure.
A disaster recovery approach with defined RTO/RPO is present for critical data/workloads.
Dependent-service failures are isolated (retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, dead-letter queues) rather than cascading.
A backup strategy exists for stateful data with a defined restore process.
Compute/storage choices match the actual workload pattern (e.g., serverless for spiky load) rather than over-provisioning.
Caching is used where repeated reads or expensive computations would otherwise recur.
The database/storage type matches its access pattern (e.g., not using a relational store for pure key-value lookups at scale).
Content/data delivery accounts for geographic distribution of users where relevant (CDN or regional deployment).
Cost tracking/tagging/budgets are defined so spend is attributable and boundable.
Resources scale down/to zero with demand rather than running at fixed capacity for variable load.
Storage has a lifecycle/retention policy rather than indefinite accumulation at full-cost tiers.
Provisioning model (on-demand vs reserved/provisioned) matches the workload's actual usage predictability.
Managed/serverless services are used where feasible to improve utilization over self-managed idle infrastructure.
Data retention/storage footprint is minimized to what's needed rather than retained indefinitely by default.
Region/deployment choice shows awareness of energy/carbon considerations where it doesn't conflict with other constraints.
AI-driven decisions that affect people can be explained at a level appropriate to the audience.
AI outputs are evaluated for unjustified variation across populations/segments where the use case involves consequential decisions.
LLM outputs are grounded (RAG, validation, citation) rather than relying on unverified generation for factual claims.
PII flowing through AI components is identified and protected (minimization, masking, or encryption).
AI-specific threats (prompt injection, data poisoning, model extraction) are considered, not just traditional infra security.
An incident response path exists specifically for AI failures (bad output, hallucination, misuse), not just general system incidents.
AI models/outputs are validated (testing, red-teaming, or human review) before being relied upon in production.
Cost per AI call/decision is knowable or estimable, not opaque.
Cheaper/smaller models are used for simple tasks, reserving expensive models for tasks that need them.
Repeated or semantically similar AI queries are cached rather than always re-invoking the model.
Data residency/location constraints are explicit and enforced by design, not left implicit.
Foundation model/vendor dependency is acknowledged with some consideration of switching cost or exit path.
AI provider calls are abstracted behind an internal interface rather than tightly coupled to one vendor's SDK throughout the codebase.
Consequential AI decisions retain a human review/override point rather than being fully autonomous.
End users/operators have a defined path to understand and correctly use the AI system's outputs.
Design choices (model size, caching, batching) that reduce cost also incidentally reduce AI inference energy footprint.
Each AI model/component in the design has a clear named owner and purpose.
AI decisions/outputs are logged with enough context (input, model version, output) to be reconstructed later.
It's clear who is accountable when the AI produces an incorrect or harmful output.
